entities.name: Kela
entities.description: One of the Chensal Arbiter Twins of the Jeskai, born in the morning and tied to innocence; she secretly doubts that she truly knows verdicts.

entities.name: Dar
entities.description: Kela's twin brother, an Arbiter Twin born in the evening and tied to guilt, who cares most about how the twins are perceived.

entities.name: Chensal Twins
entities.description: The Jeskai Arbiter Twins Kela and Dar, who judge trials in Jeskai villages by lighting or not lighting lamps in separate towers.

entities.name: Elder Ngabo
entities.description: The white-braided elder of Jigme Village who welcomes the twins and is poisoned at the celebration feast.

entities.name: Lotse Taring
entities.description: A raw, rangy man tried for stealing nine baskets of apples from Jigme Village's reserve, later blamed for poisoning the elder.

entities.name: The girl from the tree
entities.description: A watchful Jigme child who admires the twins, explains the dragon's eye mark, and helps Kela find her resolve.

entities.name: Jigme Village
entities.description: A Jeskai village known for its fabrics, with a court, a Tower of Innocence, a Tower of Guilt, and a square.

entities.name: Jigme Square
entities.description: The village square of Jigme where the twins stand on a low wooden platform.

entities.name: Jigme Tower of Innocence
entities.description: The tower where Kela chooses to light or not light her lamp.

entities.name: Tower of Guilt
entities.description: The separate tower where Dar lights or does not light his lamp.

entities.name: Jeskai
entities.description: The clan of Tarkir whose village justice rests on the Arbiter Twins and the Rules of the Reeds.

entities.name: Rules of the Reeds
entities.description: The Jeskai law that guarantees any Jeskai accused of murder a trial.

entities.name: Ritual of Arbiter Twins
entities.description: A meditation of slow movements and chanting in which the twins hear a trial and connect to truth and justice.

entities.name: Combat of Clarity
entities.description: An old, unused Arbiter Twin tradition of single combat when the twins disagree on a verdict, won by the twin with greater clarity.

entities.name: Dragon's eye
entities.description: The bright forehead mark of the Arbiter Twins, a symbol of cunning and of a path to enlightenment.

entities.name: Cori Mountain Stronghold
entities.description: A Jeskai stronghold where Kela's mentor taught her to believe in herself.

events.summary: Kela and Dar walk toward Jigme Village to arbitrate a theft case while village children stare at their glowing dragon's eye marks.
events.quote: A handful of Jigme Village children were racing toward them along the far bank of the babbling river.

events.summary: A girl in a tree falls when her branch breaks but lands like a cat and shyly smiles at Kela.
events.quote: She landed soundlessly in a crouch like a cat on the side of the path.

events.summary: Dar scolds Kela for smiling and speaking, insisting the twins' justice rests on how they are perceived.
events.quote: You shall not show emotion. What we do, it's all about perception, Kela.

events.summary: Elder Ngabo welcomes the Arbiter Twins to Jigme in the square.
events.quote: I am Elder Ngabo. You honor us with your presence, Arbiter Twins.

events.summary: The court hears the case against Lotse Taring, accused of stealing nine baskets of apples; Kela and Dar listen in deep meditation.
events.quote: Nine baskets of apples had been stolen from the Village reserve.

events.summary: Waking in the Tower of Innocence, Kela does not know the verdict, feeling like a fraud, but decides to light her lamp, then changes her mind.
events.quote: But the only thing she felt in her soul was the weight of deception.

events.summary: Kela leaves her lamp unlit; Dar lights his, and the villagers declare Lotse guilty.
events.quote: Lotse was guilty. Dar had lit his lamp.

events.summary: At the celebration, Elder Ngabo drinks apple soup and dies, apparently poisoned.
events.quote: She raised her hands to her neck, clawing wildly, her face turning gray.

events.summary: The villagers blame Lotse for poisoning the elder and storm the prison to kill him.
events.quote: She was poisoned!" This voice was loud and sure. "It was the apples!

events.summary: Kela leaps between Lotse and a warrior's sword, demanding that he receive a trial.
events.quote: He should have a trial," she whispered.

events.summary: Kela invokes the Rules of the Reeds, and Dar reluctantly agrees to a quick judgment before the mob has Lotse's head.
Kela, locked in her tower, lights her lamp of innocence, producing two flames.
events.quote: Then she lit wick. The lamp of innocence ignited.

events.summary: The mob storms the towers, and Kela escapes out the window on the air currents, pursued by Dar.
events.quote: Kela sprang out through the window.

events.summary: Dar claims to know the judgment and knocks Kela from the air; she falls to the ground and refuses to concede.
events.quote: She lost her footing and her control and she plummeted to the ground.

events.summary: The twins fight the Combat of Clarity, and Kela, seeing everything clearly, defeats Dar.
events.quote: Kela leapt into a spinning strike and landed in a crouch on the ground with her knee on Dar's chest and her blade at his throat.

events.summary: Kela spares Dar and offers him balance, and the twins stand before the villagers as equals.
events.quote: For the first time, they stood together before the villagers as equals.

events.summary: Dar announces that Lotse will have a fair trial, and the girl from the tree rings the gong.
events.quote: The man will have a fair trial," Dar said.

relations.note: Twin siblings; Dar was born the evening before Kela's morning birth.
relations.quote: Although they were twins, he had been born first—first by a day.

relations.note: Kela is the innocence half of the Arbiter Twins.
relations.quote: Being born in the morning light was the reason she was innocence

relations.note: Dar is the guilt half of the Arbiter Twins.
relations.quote: And Dar's birth in the darkness of night was the reason he was guilt
The village elder, a woman with a tight, white braid running down to her ankles, bowed to them.

relations.note: They clash over the verdict and fight, before reconciling.
relations.quote: We will fight, brother. For the judgment of this moment, we will fight.

relations.note: He is tried and jailed in Jigme Village.
relations.quote: Today, we hear the case of Lotse Taring against the Jigme Village.

relations.note: The girl's gaze steadies Kela and she rings the gong at the end.
relations.quote: And the girl from the tree was holding Kela to her part in that moment.
